questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A town council estimated the costs and benefits of operating a bus service in 2015 and 2016. These are shown in the table. 2015 2016 $000 $000 private costs 2000 2200 external costs 500 900 private benefits 1500 2300 external benefits 1000 800 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Between 2015 and 2016, social costs fell and social benefits rose.
options.B: Between 2015 and 2016, social costs rose and social benefits fell.
options.C: In both years, positive externalities exceeded negative externalities.
options.D: In both years, social costs equalled social benefits.

questions.questionText: At major sporting events, unofficial markets occur where tickets originally sold by the event organiser are resold at prices higher than the original ticket price. What might be the conclusion of an economist considering these markets?

options.A: Allocation of tickets by ballot would be preferable.
options.B: The market for the resold tickets is more equitable.
options.C: The new allocation of tickets better reflects consumers’ utility.
options.D: This is a case of monopoly exploitation.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the operation of the law of variable proportions?

options.A: As all factors are increased in proportion, the marginal cost of production increases.
options.B: As all factors are increased in proportion, total product rises at a diminishing rate.
options.C: As more of a variable factor is added to a fixed factor, the marginal cost of production diminishes.
options.D: As more of a variable factor is added to a fixed factor, total product rises at a diminishing rate.

Firms can grow internally or externally. What is a characteristic of external growth?

options.A: direct investment in productive facilities in foreign countries
options.B: growth that results in external economies benefiting other firms
options.C: growth that results from mergers with, or acquisitions of, other firms
options.D: the financing of investment by the issue of bonds rather than retained profits

options.A: shifts to right shifts to right shifts up unchanged
options.B: shifts to right shifts to right unchanged shifts up
options.C: unchanged unchanged shifts up unchanged
options.D: unchanged unchanged unchanged shifts up

questions.questionText: What would encourage an increase in the number of small firms?

options.A: increasing government regulation of conditions in the workplace
options.B: more risk-averse (safety first) lending policies by banks
options.C: stronger government laws against the growth of monopoly
options.D: tougher penalties in the case of personal bankruptcy

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. cost, revenue MC AC MR AR O output The firm changes its objective from sales revenue maximisation to profit maximisation. How will this affect the following groups in the short run? customers workers

options.A: benefit benefit
options.B: benefit lose
options.C: lose benefit
options.D: lose lose

questions.questionText: The firms in an industry decide to collude informally and follow a price leader. What will reduce the likelihood that the collusion will succeed?

options.A: The firms produce close substitutes.
options.B: The firms have similar cost structures.
options.C: There are low barriers to entry into the industry.
options.D: There are only a few firms in the industry.

questions.questionText: The theory of contestable markets can be applied to

options.A: monopolistic competition, monopoly and oligopoly.
options.B: monopolistic competition only.
options.C: monopoly and oligopoly only.
options.D: monopoly only.

questions.questionText: According to the law of diminishing returns, what happens as more of a variable factor is combined with a fixed factor?

options.A: An increase in the price of the variable factor will eventually result in an increase in production costs.
options.B: A reduction in the quality of the variable factor will eventually result in an increase in production costs.
options.C: Fewer units of the variable factor will be needed to produce equal increases in output.
options.D: The proportions in which the factors are combined will eventually result in progressively smaller increases in output.

questions.questionText: Firm X is considering whether to co-operate with its rival so that their joint profit is $4000 a month ($2000 each). It calculated that, if it did not co-operate, its own profit would be $2800 a month provided it kept all its customers itself. However, if its rival undercut X’s price and took some of X’s customers then X’s profit would be $1200. It has no knowledge of what the rival’s policy will be. What describes the situation that the firm is facing?

options.A: monopoly profit maximisation
options.B: principal agent problem
options.C: prisoner’s dilemma
options.D: satisficing

questions.questionText: Governments intent on improving living standards for individuals with low incomes sometimes impose rent controls (maximum prices) on houses rented from private landlords. What might be the effects of rent controls in the long run?

options.A: The long-run supply of rental houses will contract.
options.B: The number of unoccupied privately rented houses will increase over time.
options.C: The price of owner-occupied houses will increase.
options.D: There will be no effect on the supply of the rental housing.

questions.questionText: In certain countries benefits are provided to individuals on low income. As their income rises the benefits are reduced and income tax has to be paid. What can result from this?

options.A: price stabilisation
options.B: poverty trap
options.C: replacement ratio
options.D: unemployment trap

questions.questionText: What would help a trade union to negotiate an increase in the wage rates of its members without causing a reduction in the numbers employed?

options.A: Labour costs are a major proportion of total costs.
options.B: The demand for the labour employed is elastic.
options.C: The demand for the good produced is elastic.
options.D: The demand for the good is increasing.

What could lead to an increase in the size of a country’s labour force?

options.A: a decrease in unemployment
options.B: a decrease in the retirement age
options.C: an increase in the participation rate
options.D: an increase in the school-leaving age

questions.questionText: The table gives unemployment rates (%) for four countries in 1993 and 2002. UK Japan France Italy 1993 10.5 2.5 11.4 10.1 2002 5.0 5.4 8.8 8.5 What can be deduced from the table?

options.A: France had the lowest rate of employment in both years.
options.B: Italy had the most employed people in 2002.
options.C: Japan more than doubled its labour productivity between 1993 and 2002.
options.D: The UK created the most jobs between 1993 and 2002.

options.A: a decrease of 1%
options.B: a decrease of 2%
options.C: an increase of 2%
options.D: an increase of 3%

questions.questionText: What will cause a fall in the quantity of money demanded?

options.A: a rise in interest rates
options.B: a rise in national income
options.C: a rise in the price level
options.D: a rise in wealth

questions.questionText: What is not included in the measurement of national income?

options.A: dividends paid to shareholders
options.B: overtime payments
options.C: rents from government-owned houses
options.D: welfare benefit payments

questions.questionText: Which row correctly identifies net injections into a country’s circular flow of income? government expenditure savings exports > taxation > investment > imports

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: yes yes no

questions.questionText: Rapid economic growth is claimed by some to harm the environment. Which outcome would not harm the environment?

options.A: the greater mobility of workers resulting from increased vehicle ownership
options.B: the increased levels of income that reduce fertility rates and family size
options.C: the relocation of workers from agricultural to manufacturing employment
options.D: the use of improved technology to access previously inaccessible natural resources

questions.questionText: A country has labour shortages in some areas and high unemployment in others. Which government policy would help remove this imbalance?

options.A: abandoning national wage rates in favour of local agreements
options.B: granting subsidies to exporting firms
options.C: increasing welfare payments to the unemployed
options.D: reducing government expenditure and increasing taxation

questions.questionText: Which is likely to hinder a supply-side stimulus to the economy?

options.A: an imposition of maximum hours in a working week
options.B: an increase in public sector spending
options.C: the provision of new training schemes
options.D: the relaxation of import controls on raw materials

questions.questionText: What is most likely to influence subsequent increases in national income as a result of a government policy of reduced interest rates?

options.A: marginal cost
options.B: marginal efficiency of capital
options.C: marginal product
options.D: marginal utility

questions.questionText: What might influence the ability of a government to use income taxation to redistribute income from richer to poorer groups?

options.A: the Laffer curve
options.B: the Law of diminishing returns
options.C: the Pareto principle
